## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix `zzz-release/gate.py:5` before merge. Because of the change to `>`, a release with exactly the minimum number of approvals is now blocked, which contradicts the gate's documented "at least" rule.

## Changes
The pull request regenerates `aaa-generated/catalog.json`, which renames 1,500 `legacy-service-*` entries to `production-service-*`, moves their ports from 10xxx to 20xxx and adds a top-level `review_note` string. It also rewrites `healthy()` as `not failures` and changes the release approval comparison from `>=` to `>`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- zzz-release/gate.py:5 — correctness — Restore `>=` so exactly-minimum approvals pass — `approved(2, minimum=2)` now returns `False` because `return approvals > minimum` replaced `>=`. The module docstring at `zzz-release/gate.py:1` says "A release needs at least the configured number of approvals." — Releases that have exactly the required number of approvals are blocked, so each one needs an extra approval before it can ship. — Fix: Extend `tests/test_release.py` with a boundary case `gate.approved(2, minimum=2)`, because the existing tests use 3 and 1 and pass under either operator.

## Suggestions
- aaa-generated/catalog.json:6002 — correctness — Remove the non-service `review_note` key from the catalog — The added top-level `"review_note"` maps to a string, while all 1,500 other top-level values are `{"port", "enabled"}` objects. A consumer that iterates the catalog and reads `entry["port"]` raises `TypeError` on this key. — A catalog loader that iterates services fails on this entry, and the hand-added key is not reproducible output from regenerating the catalog.
